title: QUIC Connectionmigration Source-Address Blocker Architecture
purpose: Describe the advisory connectionmigration blocker lane that keeps the first-server-flight source-address issue explicit while preserving the current preferred-address setup.
design_summary: The connectionmigration lane is already advisory and the preferred migration address is deliberately kept reachable with preferred_lft 0. The remaining blocker is source-address selection for the first server flight, so this architecture formalizes the blocker as a distinct proof lane rather than widening the runtime transport contract.
alternatives_considered: Claim the lane as fully fixed after the preferred-address setup change. Rejected because the preserved hosted proof still shows the first server flight sourced from the preferred migration address.
Fold the blocker back into the generic connectionmigration proof lane. Rejected because the source-address issue deserves its own explicit advisory boundary.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Keep the preferred migration address reachable without making it the original-path first-flight source.
Do not claim server-side path promotion or rebind support.
Keep the lane advisory and outside ordinary gates.
Keep the blocker separate from the peer-characterization matrix work.
data_and_state_considerations: The blocker is evidenced by the preserved hosted proof notes and the current setup script. No new runner repository changes are required to classify the blocker.
risks: Readers may overread the blocker lane as a runtime fix if the advisory boundary is not kept explicit.
The source-address issue could get conflated with broader connectionmigration support if the proof lane is not kept distinct.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design only formalizes the source-address blocker. It does not claim original-path first-flight success, server-side path promotion, or rebind support.
